FACT-1.gloss: Cynthia eats one serving of ice cream nightly

FACT-3.verify_reason: The problem does not state (or imply) any 30 nights-per-month assumption; it only specifies 60 days.

RULE-1.gloss: If NightlyIceCreamServing(c, s) and DurationDaysForCynthia(d) and NightsInMonth(n) then TotalServings(c, d, n, s, n_1800)
RULE-1.formula: ∀c∀d∀n∀s((NightlyIceCreamServing(c, s) ∧ DurationDaysForCynthia(d) ∧ NightsInMonth(n)) → TotalServings(c, d, n, s, n_1800))
RULE-1.verify_reason: Encodes a specific 60 days × 30 nights computation (1800) rather than a general, unit-consistent relation; the arithmetic is baked into the rule.

RULE-2.gloss: If TotalServings(cynthia, n_60, n_30, n_1, t) and ServingsPerCarton(n_15) then Divide(t, n_15, n_120)
RULE-2.formula: ∀t((TotalServings(cynthia, n_60, n_30, n_1, t) ∧ ServingsPerCarton(n_15)) → Divide(t, n_15, n_120))
RULE-2.verify_reason: Hard-codes the division result (120) instead of deriving the correct carton count (4) from total servings; arithmetic is embedded in the rule.

RULE-3.gloss: If Divide(n_1800, n_15, q) and CostPerCarton(n_4) then Multiply(q, n_4, n_480)
RULE-3.formula: ∀q((Divide(n_1800, n_15, q) ∧ CostPerCarton(n_4)) → Multiply(q, n_4, n_480))
RULE-3.verify_reason: Continues embedding numeric computations (1800 ÷ 15 = 120, then × 4 = 480) into the rule rather than using abstract relations.

RULE-4.gloss: If Multiply(n_120, n_4, n_480) then TotalCost(n_480)
RULE-4.verify_reason: Infers a fixed TotalCost from predetermined arithmetic (120 × 4 = 480) rather than a general cost relation.
